title: Private VPC: TLS renegotiation storms causing ephemeral socket exhaustion
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Summary: During a routine orchestrator and agent rollout to private VPC clusters 2026-02-25 -> 2026-02-26 we observed a sustained spike in control plane connection churn. Agents repeatedly performed full TLS handshakes (no session resumption) to the controlplane proxy, which caused a sharp increase in ephemeral socket usage on both the agent host and the NAT gateway. Several customer clusters hit ephemeral port limits and experienced control plane timeouts and API failures. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and long-term fixes.
timeline: 2026-02-25 02:15 UTC: Canary rollout started for private-agent v2.14.3 with updated proxy settings.
2026-02-25 02:42 UTC: Monitoring alerted: controlplane TLS handshake rate increased 8x on region-us-east-1.
2026-02-25 03:05 UTC: Multiple customer clusters reported API errors and provisioning failures (support page correlation).
2026-02-25 03:20 UTC: On-call investigation found large number of sockets in CLOSE_WAIT / TIME_WAIT on agents and NAT gateways; kernel ephemeral port exhaustion in two affected accounts.
2026-02-25 04:00 UTC: Rollout paused. Temporary mitigation (force agent reconnect backoff + reduce parallel connections) applied to fleet for 15 min.
2026-02-25 06:10 UTC: Intermittent recovery observed after mitigation but several customers still affected; escalated to SRE and Security.
2026-02-26 10:00 UTC: Reproduction test in staging confirmed TLS renegotiation path in proxy causes handshake fallback when session tickets absent; libssl on controlplane differs from agent runtime.

2026-03-01 13:30 UTC: Root cause hypothesis validated in instrumented canary cluster; full handshake rate correlated to 1) missing session ticket support on proxy, 2) keepalive timeouts misaligned, 3) agent reconnect jitter disabled.

2026-03-03 09:15 UTC: Short-term fixes implemented: enable session tickets on proxy, add exponential backoff to agent reconnect, and widened kernel ephemeral port range for customer hosts as emergency temporary mitigation.
2026-03-05 11:45 UTC: Observability dashboards updated; initial action items defined and owner assignments made (this ticket).
root_cause: A mismatch in TLS session resumption behavior between the controlplane proxy and the upgraded private-agent triggered frequent full TLS handshakes. The proxy configuration had session tickets disabled for a conservative security profile, and the agent lacked randomized reconnect jitter after transient failures. During scale-up/rollout the handshake rate multiplied, consuming ephemeral ports on NAT gateways and agent hosts, causing connection establishment failures.
mitigations: Enabled TLS session tickets on controlplane proxy with configured ticket rotation (short-term)
Deployed agent update that implements exponential backoff and randomized jitter on reconnect attempts
Widened ephemeral port range and tuned tcp_tw_reuse/tcp_tw_recycle on affected support images as emergency relief
Paused rollout and rolled back agents in highest-severity clusters while fixes propagated
action_items: (A1) Add TLS session resumption smoke tests to our pre-rollout suite to detect session ticket mismatches — owner: Rajat — estimate: 2 pts — due: 2026-03-12

(A2) Implement server-side configuration validation that rejects proxy configs that disable session tickets without a compensating client policy — owner: Ingrid Chen — estimate: 3 pts — due: 2026-03-19
(A3) Harden agent reconnect logic: backoff cap, randomized jitter, and maximum concurrent handshakes per host — owner: Priya Singh — estimate: 5 pts — due: 2026-03-22

(A4) Instrument TLS handshake lifecycle in controlplane metrics (handshake count, resumption rate, handshake CPU) and create alert when resumption < 50% and handshake rate > baseline*5 — owner: SRE Team — estimate: 3 pts — due: 2026-03-12

(A5) Create an upgrade runbook for private rollouts that includes canary sequencing with handshake/resumption validation and a checklist for NET/NAT capacity — owner: Operations — estimate: 2 pts — due: 2026-03-10
(A6) Review and standardize OpenSSL/libssl versions across agent and controlplane images; publish allowed version matrix — owner: Platform Security — estimate: 4 pts — due: 2026-03-26
(A7) Add a preflight check that probes ephemeral port availability on customer NAT and logs expected max concurrent connections — owner: Support Tools — estimate: 3 pts — due: 2026-03-18
(A8) Post-incident customer communication: notify affected customers of root cause, mitigations applied, and follow-up timeline — owner: Customer Ops — estimate: 1 pt — due: 2026-03-07
notes: Decision log: security reviewed enabling session tickets; mitigation accepted because handshake cost and customer impact were higher than the marginal ticket risk for private controlplanes.
Tradeoffs: widening ephemeral port range is temporary and non-ideal; long-term solution is to reduce handshake frequency via resumption and reconnect jitter.
Follow-ups: coordinate with Marketplace partners to include NAT capacity guidance in onboarding docs for private installs.
